item.title: 로봇 팔던 中 기업들이 벤처투자에 수천억원 쏟아붓는 이유 [차이나 워치] - 한국경제
item.description:
요약

  • 로봇 팔던 中 기업들이 벤처투자에 수천억원 쏟아붓는 이유 [차이나 워치]
  • 중국 휴머노이드(인간형) 로봇 선두기업들이 스타트업 투자에 잇따라 뛰어들고 있다.
  • 중국 로봇기업들은 산업 생태계 확보가 향후 경쟁력을 좌우할 수 있다는 판단에 이같은 투자에 적극 나서고 있다.

본문

로봇 팔던 中 기업들이 벤처투자에 수천억원 쏟아붓는 이유 [차이나 워치]

中 유니트리·즈위안, 이젠 스타트업 투자까지

"유망 기술부터 선점하자"…AI 생태계 장악 나섰다

중국 휴머노이드(인간형) 로봇 선두기업들이 스타트업 투자에 잇따라 뛰어들고 있다. 로봇 제조와 기술 개발에 집중하던 기업들이 인공지능(AI) 반도체와 센서, 로봇용 손, 데이터 등 핵심 기술을 보유한 신생 기업에 직접 자금을 투입하기 시작한 것이다.

중국 로봇산업의 투자 열기가 올 하반기 들어 주춤한 상황에서도 선두기업들은 오히려 투자 범위를 확대하고 있다. 유망 기술과 공급망을 선점해 장기적인 경쟁 우위를 확보하려는 움직임으로 풀이된다.

14일 중국 매체들을 종합해보면 중국 휴머노이드 로봇기업 즈위안(애지봇)는 최근 기존 스타트업 육성 프로그램인 창업투자 A계획을 전면 확대했다. 지난해 8월 시작된 이 프로그램은 세계 각국의 초기 창업기업을 대상으로 3년간 50개 이상의 프로젝트를 육성하는 것이 목표다.

즈위안은 지난 1년여간 20개 이상의 기업에 투자했다. 투자 대상은 센서와 반도체, 로봇용 정밀 손, 생체모방 로봇, 데이터 수집, 피지컬 AI 모델 등 로봇산업 전반에 걸쳐 있다. 대부분 창업 초기인 시드 투자나 엔젤투자, 시리즈A 단계의 기업들이다.

덩타이화 즈위안 창업자 겸 회장·최고경영자(CEO)는 최근 산업 행사에서 투자 대상 기업들의 기업가치가 연평균 17배 상승했다고 밝혔다.

즈위안은 2026년 혁신의 날 행사에서 투자 영역을 차세대 AI 인프라와 차세대 AI 모델, 우주·생명과학 분야까지 확대하겠다고 발표하기도 했다. 로봇 제조에 필요한 기술 확보와 함께 피지컬 AI의 응용 영역을 넓히겠다는 전략이다.

스타트업에 자체 하드웨어와 산업 현장, 데이터를 개방하는 지원 프로그램도 공개했다. 앞서 발표한 생태계 발전 계획에는 향후 5년간 20억위안(약 4000억원) 이상을 투입하기로 했다. 연구개발과 인재 양성, 협력기업 육성, 개발자 커뮤니티 운영 등에 사용할 예정이다.

유니트리·즈위안은 돈 보따리 풀었다

경쟁사인 유니트리도 투자 경쟁에 합류했다. 유니트리는 최근 중국 벤처캐피털(VC) 세쿼이아차이나와 손잡고 공동 창업투자 프로그램인 산위창계획을 출범시켰다. 로봇 응용 기술과 핵심 부품, 피지컬 AI 등 첨단 기술 분야의 초기 스타트업을 발굴할 계획이다. 유니트리의 엔지니어링 역량과 세쿼이아차이나의 투자 전문성을 결합하는 방식이다.

유니트리는 별도로 200개 이상의 로봇 생태계 기업을 육성하는 계획도 추진하고 있다. 로봇용 소프트웨어와 데이터·시뮬레이션 플랫폼, 핵심 부품, AI 알고리즘, 해외 판매망 등이 지원 대상이다. 향후 5년간 예상되는 협력 규모는 수십억위안에 달한다.

또 다른 중국 로봇기업 싱하이투(갤럭시아)도 투자사 케세이캐피털과 공동으로 스타트업 육성 프로그램을 출범시켰다. 향후 5년간 10억위안을 투입해 피지컬 AI 분야 초기 기업에 자금과 기술, 산업 자원을 제공할 계획이다.

중국 로봇기업들은 산업 생태계 확보가 향후 경쟁력을 좌우할 수 있다는 판단에 이같은 투자에 적극 나서고 있다. 휴머노이드 로봇의 상용화가 아직 초기 단계인 만큼 핵심 부품과 AI 학습 데이터, 알고리즘 기술을 안정적으로 확보하는 것이 중요해졌다는 분석이다.

가오궁로봇산업연구소의 차이빙전 소장은 "피지컬 AI가 아직 초기 발전 단계에 있어 생태계 협력기업을 육성하는 것이 산업과 공급망 발전에 도움이 된다"고 설명했다.

다만 투자 확대가 실제 경쟁력으로 이어질지는 미지수다. 왕한 야오린창투 파트너는 일부 로봇기업의 투자가 부품 구매계약과 연계될 가능성을 지적했다. 투자 대상 기업에서 제품을 구매해 매출을 늘려주는 방식이다.

그는 "시장가격에 따른 정상적인 구매라면 건전하지만 투자 이전에 구매 규모를 약정했다면 투자를 통해 매출을 촉진하는 성격이 강하다"고 설명했다. 이어 "이런 투자가 산업 경쟁력으로 이어질지는 건강한 공급망 관계를 형성할 수 있는지에 달려 있다"고 강조했다.

베이징=김은정 특파원 kej@hankyung.com

출처: 한국경제

item.title: [사이언스영상] 로봇도 롤러스케이트를? 바퀴로 달리는 휴머노이드 - DongA Science
item.description:
요약

  • 현대차그룹의 휴머노이드 로봇 ’아틀라스‘가 발 대신 바퀴를 달았다.
  • 현대차그룹 산하 미국 로봇 기업 보스턴다이내믹스는 아틀라스의 두 발을 바퀴로 바꾼 실험 영상을 현지시간 11월 9일 유튜브에 올렸다.
  • 보스턴다이내믹스는 블로그와 영상에서 ”바퀴 달린 아틀라스는 제품이 아니라 연구용 시험대“라며 ”모터를 한계까지 밀어붙이는 게 이번 실험의 목적이었다“고 밝혔다.

본문

롤러 타는 현대차 로봇. 씨즈팀 제공

현대차그룹의 휴머노이드 로봇 ’아틀라스‘가 발 대신 바퀴를 달았다. 바닥을 미끄러지듯 드리프트하고, 360° 회전 점프도 해낸다. 현대차그룹 산하 미국 로봇 기업 보스턴다이내믹스는 아틀라스의 두 발을 바퀴로 바꾼 실험 영상을 현지시간 11월 9일 유튜브에 올렸다.

연구팀은 가상 공간에서 먼저 동작을 훈련시켰다. 이 동작은 실제 로봇에서도 거의 그대로 통했고, 360° 점프는 첫 시도에 성공했다. 보스턴다이내믹스는 블로그와 영상에서 ”바퀴 달린 아틀라스는 제품이 아니라 연구용 시험대“라며 ”모터를 한계까지 밀어붙이는 게 이번 실험의 목적이었다“고 밝혔다.

※출처 : Boston Dynamics / YouTube

item.title: Students Welcome CU Denver’s Newest Robot - CU Denver News
item.description:
본문

Lynx joined a gathering of CU Denver’s robots in North Classroom the morning of Thursday, Nov. 12. The group, which included the robotic dogs from the Civil Engineering department, welcomed the university’s latest non-human community member: a humanoid robot from Unitree Robotics. It was jointly purchased by the Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Science departments, with additional funding from the dean’s office of the College of Engineering, Design and Computing. The robot will be used for research, educational, and recruitment purposes across the college.

The acquisition is part of the college’s broader initiative to advance robotics research and education through interdisciplinary collaboration. The robot is programmable and can be equipped with AI capabilities. “We want to study how this human robot is working,” said Professor of Electrical Engineering Jae-Do Park. “Ultimately, we want to build our own.” Park also plans to use the robot in robotics courses in the college.

Learn more about CU Denver’s engineering programs here. Students interested in robotics, AI, and related topics can find relevant student organizations to get involved with and meet like-minded peers here.

출처: CU Denver News

item.title: [로봇 온사이트] 휴머노이드 시대, 유럽의 자리는 - 더구루
item.description:
요약

  • 모니터 속 텍스트와 스마트폰 액정을 벗어난 인공지능(AI)이 마침내 '육체'를 얻어 산업과 일상의 '현장(On-Site)'으로 뛰어들기 시작했다.
  • 다만 미국 대비 열세인 투자 자본력과 빠른 개발 속도를 앞세운 중국 추격, 산업 현장 검증 데이터 부족은 유럽이 넘어야 할 구조적 한계로 꼽힌다.
  • 유럽 휴머노이드 산업의 가장 뚜렷한 강점은 자동차·부품·조선 등 전통 제조 대기업이 투자자이자 핵심 부품 공급사, 위탁생산 파트너, 초기 도입 고객사로 직접 결합한 수직 생태계다.

본문

모니터 속 텍스트와 스마트폰 액정을 벗어난 인공지능(AI)이 마침내 '육체'를 얻어 산업과 일상의 '현장(On-Site)'으로 뛰어들기 시작했다. 껍데기에 불과했던 기계가 고도화된 지능을 얻어 인간과 공존하기 시작한 것이다. 더구루는 로봇의 종류부터 핵심 부품, 기술적 난제, 신제품, 시장 트렌드까지 실체화된(Embodied) AI가 주도하는 거대한 변화의 '발자취'를 따라가 볼 예정이다. -편집자주-

[더구루=홍성일 기자] 글로벌 휴머노이드 로봇·피지컬 AI 패권 경쟁이 격화하는 가운데 유럽 로봇 산업이 전통 제조 대기업과 수직 결합을 무기로 상용화 활로를 모색하고 있다. 유럽 주요 제조사는 현지 휴머노이드 스타트업 지분 투자와 부품 공급, 위탁생산, 공장 라인 투입을 동시에 추진하며 생태계 확장에 나섰다.

다만 미국 대비 열세인 투자 자본력과 빠른 개발 속도를 앞세운 중국 추격, 산업 현장 검증 데이터 부족은 유럽이 넘어야 할 구조적 한계로 꼽힌다. 유럽 산업계는 자체 촉각 센서·실용 하드웨어 기술과 엄격한 데이터 거버넌스를 발판 삼아 글로벌 협력·현장 실증을 병행하며 독자 입지를 다지고 있다.

유럽 휴머노이드 산업의 가장 뚜렷한 강점은 자동차·부품·조선 등 전통 제조 대기업이 투자자이자 핵심 부품 공급사, 위탁생산 파트너, 초기 도입 고객사로 직접 결합한 수직 생태계다. 독일 자동차 부품사 셰플러는 독일 뉴라 로보틱스, 영국 휴머노이드AI, 스웨덴 헥사곤 로보틱스 3개 사와 모두 전략적 파트너십을 체결하고 액추에이터 부품을 공급한다. 보쉬는 영국 휴머노이드 산업용 로봇 'HMND 01' 유럽 위탁생산과 지분 투자를 동시에 맡았다.

완성차와 조선 현장 실증도 구체화하고 있다. 르노는 완더크래프트와 손잡고 내년 말까지 프랑스·스페인 공장에 휴머노이드 350대를 배치할 계획이다. BMW는 라이프치히 공장에 헥사곤 로보틱스 'AEON'을 투입했으며, 이탈리아 국영 조선사 핀칸티에리는 제너레이티브 바이오닉스 'Gene.01'을 조선소 용접 실증에 활용하고 있다.

유럽 휴머노이드 산업의 약점도 뚜렷하다. 미국 대비 투자 자본력 열세, 중국 대비 느린 개발 속도와 국가 주도 기획력 격차, 물리 세계의 검증된 산업 데이터 부족, 대도시 외곽·지방 제조 거점 내 고급 기술 인력 확보난 등이 대표적이다.

실제로 자본 열세는 미·중과 격차를 키우는 주요 요인으로 지목된다. 뉴라 로보틱스가 지난 6월 시리즈 C 투자 라운드에서 14억 달러(약 1조8700억원), 휴머노이드AI가 시리즈 A로 1억5200만 달러(약 2030억원)를 확보하며 대규모 자본이 유입되고 있으나, 전반적인 자본 동원력에서는 미국에 미치지 못한다는 평가다.

유럽은 기업과 학계가 함께하는 개방형 협력 체제 구축 등에서 해법을 찾고 있다.

업계 관계자는 "유럽은 미국보다 자본력이 부족하고, 중국은 모든 주체가 동시에 움직이는 재즈 밴드처럼 병렬적으로 제품을 개발하며 5개년 계획 같은 제도적 기획이 산업 전체를 한 방향으로 이끈다"며 "미국과 중국에서 배울 것은 배우고 개방형 협력 체계를 기반으로 역량을 결합해 유럽만의 모델을 구축해야 한다"고 말했다.

출처: 더구루

item.title: Social Robots Match Human Storytellers in Sustaining Young Learners’ Engagement - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Impact of social robots on multidimensional learning engagement in early childhood storytelling
  • Article Title: Let’s listen and tell a story together: social robot and multidimensional learning engagement among young learners
  • Let’s listen and tell a story together: social robot and multidimensional learning engagement among young learners. AI, Brain and Child, 1(1), Article 5. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44436-025-00006-2

본문

In an experimental evaluation involving young children learning English as a second language, researchers found that an interactive social robot matched a human storyteller in sustaining children’s behavioral engagement across storytelling tasks, significantly outperforming a tablet computer. Published in the journal AI, Brain and Child, the comparative study examined seventy-seven children aged five to seven as they participated in sequential listening and collaborative co-telling activities. While prior investigations into child-robot interaction have predominantly focused on passive story reception, this investigation tested how an embodied robotic agent influences multidimensional learning engagement—spanning behavioral, cognitive, and emotional axes—when children transition from listening to actively co-narrating a story. The researchers discovered that while children showed equivalent initial engagement across all three conditions, the social robot maintained behavioral involvement when the activity shifted toward interactive co-telling, mirroring a human educator. The empirical findings provide novel evidence for integrating embodied conversational robotics into early childhood language instruction.

The theoretical foundation of the research rests on Social Agency Theory, which posits that technological agents possessing humanlike physical, verbal, and nonverbal cues encourage learners to interpret their pedagogical interactions as authentic social encounters. Social robots operate within embodied physical environments, contrasting sharply with conventional screen-based tools such as tablets. Researchers have noted that humanoid and semi-humanoid designs featuring expressive faces, communicative gestures, and adaptive vocalizations can adopt roles analogous to peer companions or instructional assistants. For early childhood learners, such interactive social presence is especially consequential because children at this developmental stage frequently acquire language and cognitive competencies through collaborative, playful social exchange. However, despite expanding interest in educational robotics, comparisons testing interactive storytelling across physical robots, tablets, and human educators have remained scarce. Most prior literature has evaluated situations where robots delivered stories passively, leaving unresolved questions about whether robotic agents can facilitate collaborative narrative exchanges.

item.description:

  • LeBlanc stressed that, while robotics companies have been creating both warfare drones and household humanoid robots, Foundation is the first company to create humanoid robots specifically for warfare.
  • "She has called us out on, you know, ‘Do the Trumps think that the Pentagon is their own personal ATM?’ For me, this just kind of goes against all of the facts and experience that I have in it," LeBlanc said.

본문

Foundation Future Robotics, an Eric Trump-backed robotics company, became the first company to deploy humanoid robots to a combat zone when it sent its Phantom MK 1 robots to Ukraine in February.

Now in talks to ship more MK 1 units to Israel, expanding its war theater footprint, Foundation co-founder Mike LeBlanc sees a near future in which the majority of warfighting is done by robots.

"In the next five to 10 years, I would expect that humanoids, ground vehicles, drones, will be doing most of the major fighting, with humans really only doing special forces, special operations, small surgical operations on the side," LeBlanc, a former Marine Corps officer with three tours of duty in the Middle East, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.

ZELENSKYY ANNOUNCES 'THE FUTURE IS HERE' AFTER WAR'S FIRST ALL-ROBOT CAPTURE

LeBlanc stressed that, while robotics companies have been creating both warfare drones and household humanoid robots, Foundation is the first company to create humanoid robots specifically for warfare.

The MK 1 units deployed to Ukraine have a roughly 88-pound carrying capacity, making their best fit in combat situations one of a supplementary role, assisting human soldiers with ordnance, munitions loading, manual labor and other ancillary tasks.

However, LeBlanc explained that the units were simply a "proof of concept" for the broader application of humanoid robots in war, claiming that Foundation is already close to shipping out the MK 2.

"It is 6 feet tall, 185 pounds, as I say, created in my own image," LeBlanc joked.

THIS ROBOT DOG WAS MADE TO SAVE SOLDIERS' LIVES AS US RACES INTO NEW ERA OF AUTONOMOUS WARFARE

"But this thing is ready to engage by making small and medium machine guns, by engaging with enemies.

"The Mark II is going to be the biggest, fastest, strongest humanoid on the market. This robot is already able to pick me up. So, it's a much larger payload than anybody else. That allows us to do heavy industrial work, but it also lets us set up heavy machine guns, bullfrogs, etc.," LeBlanc told Fox News Digital.

ARMY CUTS HELICOPTERS, PUSHES ‘AMAZON FOR WAR’ AS DRONE COMBAT RESHAPES MILITARY

LeBlanc said Ukraine will likely be the first place the MK 2 is deployed, a fitting testing ground, he explained, as the war between Ukraine and Russia is largely being fought by machines already.

"In Ukraine, robots are very much a question of today and today's battlefield," LeBlanc explained.

PENTAGON JUMPS FROM $225M TO $55B ON DRONES AS CHEAP ATTACKS OVERWHELM US DEFENSES

He then marveled at how quickly the combat environment has shifted, contrasting today’s battlefield with those he engaged in during his tours of duty.

"It's amazing how quickly things change. I was in Afghanistan in 2012, and then again in 2013. And, at that time, they would have very small drones that it was almost like you were looking through a toilet paper roll," LeBlanc told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Humanoid Robots Could Outnumber Humans by 2083 as Long as They Start Building Each Other - ZME Science
item.description:
요약

  • The next population boom may have nothing to do with babies. It will likely happen on factory floors, as soon as humanoid robots begin helping to manufacture more robots in their own image.
  • For every million people walking the Earth today, there is roughly one human-like robot. By the end of this century, there could be many more of them than us.
  • A new mathematical study suggests that human-shaped robots or androids, if you will, could become as numerous as people by 2083, when the global human population is expected to approach 10.3 billion.

본문

The next population boom may have nothing to do with babies. It will likely happen on factory floors, as soon as humanoid robots begin helping to manufacture more robots in their own image.

For every million people walking the Earth today, there is roughly one human-like robot. By the end of this century, there could be many more of them than us.

A new mathematical study suggests that human-shaped robots or androids, if you will, could become as numerous as people by 2083, when the global human population is expected to approach 10.3 billion.

Using equations originally designed to describe how glass ages and how human populations surged over 12,000 years, the researchers found that conventional, human-run factories alone will likely never produce enough machines to match the human headcount. Instead, numerical parity hinges on achieving an industrial tipping point: when deployed androids begin manufacturing their own successors.

“For all of human history, we have counted people. We may soon need to count another population sharing the planet with us,” the researchers write in a statement accompanying the study.

Today, the global fleet of humanoid robots is still small — numbered in the tens of thousands — but major automakers, logistics giants, and tech firms are already putting these still early units to work. In warehouse distribution centers, Agility Robotics has logged tens of thousands of commercial operating hours with its bipedal Digit robots hauling totes for Amazon, while Apptronik is piloting its Apollo humanoids with Mercedes-Benz and logistics giant GXO. On automotive assembly lines, Figure AI has deployed its robots at BMW’s Spartanburg plant, Boston Dynamics is rolling out its all-electric Atlas to Hyundai facilities, and Tesla is scaling internal factory trials for its Optimus platform.

Meanwhile, Chinese manufacturers like Unitree Robotics and AgiBot are shipping thousands of lower-cost platforms for research and industrial tasks, and companies such as 1X Technologies have opened consumer preorders for home-assistant androids like NEO designed to handle basic household chores.

The growth so far is encouraging. But even a billion robots — a huge milestone — would be vastly outnumbered by the approximately 9.7 billion people expected to inhabit Earth by the turn of this century.

To explore what might happen next, physicist Alessio Zaccone of the University of Milan, mathematical biologist Thomas Tunstall of the University of Exeter, and environmental scientist Jesse Ausubel of Rockefeller University developed a model of how human and robot populations might evolve.

Their 56-page study, published as a preprint on arXiv, adapts a mathematical framework that allows growth rates to change as populations expand.

item.title: Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter - NVIDIA Developer
item.description:
요약

  • This post explains the retargeting process, the tools for refining robot motion, and the connection to policy learning.
  • From human motion to robot joint trajectories
  • You can also generate motion with MotionBricks’ SOMA human model and use SOMA Retargeter to adapt it to your robot, expanding the motion references available for downstream training.

본문

Human motion offers roboticists a great starting point for teaching humanoid robots how to move. A human demonstration captures the coordination and timing behind natural movement, from everyday actions to complex tasks. But a robot cannot simply copy the same joint motion from a human. Its proportions, joint structure, and range of motion are different, so the movement needs to be adapted to fit the robot.

The open source NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter helps you adapt human motion to your robot’s proportions and range of motion. Built around the shared human-motion representation in NVIDIA SOMA-X, it provides tools to configure your robot, refine the resulting movement, and process motion data for downstream training.

This post explains the retargeting process, the tools for refining robot motion, and the connection to policy learning.

From human motion to robot joint trajectories

Human motion can come from many sources, including a motion capture session, a video, an online dataset, or a generative model. These sources often output motion with different skeletons and file formats. Representing compatible human motion on the SOMA skeleton gives the retargeter a consistent input.

SOMA Retargeter reads a Biovision Hierarchy (BVH) animation on the SOMA base skeleton. As Figure 1 below shows, it scales motion targets to the robot’s proportions, solves for joint poses, and applies configured corrections. The output is a comma-separated values (CSV) file containing the robot’s root position, orientation, and joint angles for each frame. These trajectories describe the desired movement for a downstream learning or control system.

Sources of human motion

Developers can draw on recorded performances, reconstruct motion from video, or generate new movements:

- Motion-capture data. BONES-SEED provides a collection of human motion-capture data.

- Video reconstruction. GEM-X reconstructs whole-body 3D human motion from a single video using the SOMA body model. Its demo workflow connects video reconstruction with G1 retargeting, showing how a recorded action can become a robot motion reference.

- Motion generation. Kimodo and ARDY let developers generate human movement from text and pose constraints. Kimodo supports creating motion sequences from those descriptions, while ARDY adds interactive steering as the motion unfolds. Both offer models that generate motion on the SOMA skeleton.

Adapting motion to different humanoid robots

The SOMA Retargeter v0.2 release includes sample motions supplied by Bones from the BONES-SEED dataset, along with reference retargeting results and configurations for five humanoid robots: Unitree G1, Unitree H2, Booster T1, AgiBot X2 Ultra, and AgiBot A3T3. These examples show how joint angles and foot placement change across humanoid embodiments according to their specific proportions and range of motion. The paired human motions and robot results give you a starting point for exploring the tool and comparing your own output.

item.title: Exclusive: OpenAI disbands its stand-alone robotics team as its general models start running robots - Fortune
item.description:
요약

  • OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, moving its researchers onto other teams.
  • The company confirmed the reorganization when asked about it by Fortune. A company spokesperson said that robotics remains a core part of OpenAI’s long-term vision and portrayed the reorganization as a sign of the company’s commitment to robotics, rather than a retreat from it.
  • The company spokesperson said that despite the reorganization, OpenAI remains committed to bringing general-purpose robots into the world.

본문

OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, moving its researchers onto other teams.

The company confirmed the reorganization when asked about it by Fortune. A company spokesperson said that robotics remains a core part of OpenAI’s long-term vision and portrayed the reorganization as a sign of the company’s commitment to robotics, rather than a retreat from it.

OpenAI said it has reassigned its robotics research team to the company’s main research team, reporting to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen, while the applied robotics and hardware teams have been reassigned to the company’s larger Applied organization, which reports to OpenAI President Greg Brockman.

The change came recently enough that OpenAI had already registered a booth at CoRL, a top academic robotics conference in Austin, this week. Though the conference app and floor plan marked OpenAI’s spot, when Fortune visited booth #208, it sat empty with OpenAI’s logo nowhere to be seen.

OpenAI had a robotics team in its early days but wound it down in 2020, with cofounder Wojciech Zaremba later citing limited robot data and a more efficient path toward artificial general intelligence (AGI)—the human-like AI that has been OpenAI’s goal since its founding—through other methods. In particular, OpenAI became increasingly devoted to training ultra-large language models on vast datasets of human-written text. This is the approach that eventually yielded the company’s breakthrough product ChatGPT in late 2022.

OpenAI rebuilt a stand alone robotics team in 2024, announcing a partnership with the startup Figure to develop AI models for humanoid robots. That partnership ended in February 2025, when Figure said it would develop its own robot AI. OpenAI has said it is currently developing its own humanoid robot, with CEO Sam Altman targeting a first public demonstration in 2027.

The company spokesperson said that despite the reorganization, OpenAI remains committed to bringing general-purpose robots into the world.

The reorganization reflects a bet that is gaining traction across the AI industry: that general-purpose models built for language, code, and vision can also be used for “embodied AI”—where AI models control devices that can act in the physical world, such as robots, driverless cars, or drones. This would obviate the need to have separate robotics teams building specialized AI models just to be the digital “brains” for robots.

Researchers have seen surprising performance when connecting GPT-6 Astra to robots, directly using the general-purpose AI model to perform some robotic tasks.
